$comment: THE ONE DECLARATION of which bun this repository runs: the compiler behind
every content-addressed /a/ and /i/ URL (wrangler.jsonc builds with `bun
tools/build.ts`), and the runtime the contract suite runs under.
It lived in package.json's packageManager until 2026-09-15, and it moved
because Cloudflare's build image READS THAT FIELD and cannot resolve a canary
in it: measured with three probes on the day, a release pin builds, a dated
canary fails whether or not it carries its build sha, and removing the field
with the pin here builds and uploads a version compiled by the canary. The
image is the one reader that cannot handle the truth, so the declaration
moved to a file only this repository's own tools read. Every reader is here:
tools/lib/bun-pin.ts (readPin/writePin), .github/install-bun.sh (the shared
installer for the setup-bun action and the Workers Builds wrapper), and
bun-pin.yml, which reads it before and after a bump.
A pin is a release (`1.4.2`) or a DATED CANARY WITH ITS BUILD SHA
(`1.4.2-canary.20260913.1+09bb546`), both exact and immutable on npm. The
channel is the pin's own shape, bump-bun-pin.ts walks that channel and never
crosses; switching channels is a hand edit here plus `bun run bun:pin`.
The sha is load-bearing: a canary binary reports the NEXT release as its
--version, and Bun.revision is what proves a running bun is this pin.
There is deliberately NO packageManager in package.json any more. Putting
one back hands the image a field it will try to resolve, and the day it
names a canary the production build stops.
